newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Sun Air sale price could fall - report.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Sun Air sale price could fall - report.

text.p: The South African government is likely to receive between 50 million rand and 90 million rand for the soon-to-be privatised regional airline Sun Air, Business Report said on Wednesday.
Quoting sources close to the deal, the paper said this was far less than previous estimates of up to 200 million rand.

As the eight selected finalists considered whether to make non-binding offers for the airline ahead of Thursday's deadline, some said the scant information they were given by the government suggested that Sun Air would fetch anything between 50 million rand and 90 million rand.
The airline would also need a significant recapitalisation -- of up to 400 million rand -- to remain competitive and expand into new routes and markets, such as cargo, one source said.

The eight potential bidders shortlisted for the privatisation of the airline are Virgin Atlantic, together with six black empowerment groups; Malaysian Airline Systems Bhd ; Air France and Comair, which already has a franchise agreement with British Airways plc, together with NSA Investments Ltd.

The others are: Rethabile Consortium, consisting of black business involved in tourism; Ukhozi Sanco Consortium, consisting of the investment arm of the South African National Civic Organisation; Phoenix Venture Partners, an investment banking and emerging markets company with six black empowerment groups and Maru Investment Holdings, a black empowerment group from North-West province.
